clue.text: Fast-moving Basque play

parts.note: describes the quick court game of the Basque country, where a ball is hurled against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is the speedy wall-and-ball sport native to the Basque region of Spain and France.

clue.text: Hungry retinues put to rout

indicators.note: a routed army scatters in disorder, so the letters of the clue word are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: Starving followers of some lord are driven off the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to rout' scrambles RETINUES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a formal synonym for greedy or ravenous.

clue.text: Place at the bottom of the scale

definitions.text: Place at the bottom of the scale

parts.words: Place at the bottom of the scale
parts.note: the lowest rung, read both literally on a ladder and figuratively as the most junior position in a career or hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rung, figuratively, is the starting point of any career progression.

clue.text: A carving about right for height

indicators.note: the carving is placed around the abbreviation, as if surrounding it

parts.note: a statue is a carved figure

explanation.surface: A sculpted figure is chosen because it is the right height.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means a person's natural standing height.

clue.text: One poster picked at random to display humility, perhaps

indicators.note: letters taken at random come out in no set order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single placard is drawn by lot to show humble feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' rearranges the fifteen letters of ONE POSTER PICKED; 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example of swallowing pride.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow or set aside self-esteem, as in accepting something humbling, is a show of humility.

clue.text: Journalist probably tried nothing odd

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A reporter, one suspects, attempted something that was nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' scrambles TRIED plus O into the answer; 'probably' shows the definition is an example, since not every editor is a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor is typically a senior journalist in charge of content.

clue.text: Lincoln apprentice killed in a family quarrel

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was known as Abe
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A young assistant to the president dies during a domestic row.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Abel was murdered by his brother Cain, the first family quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's Abel was slain by his sibling Cain, a fratricide within the first family.

clue.text: Stops trading unprofitably and pays everybody off?

definitions.text: Stops trading unprofitably and pays everybody off?

parts.words: Stops trading unprofitably and pays everybody off?
parts.note: describes a business that ceases losing money and settles all its creditors, becoming solvent

explanation.definitionFit: Clearing every creditor means owing nothing, the state of solvency.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
troop out as one of the most famous fictional detectives

definitions.text: one of the most famous fictional detectives

indicators.note: the soldiers are turned out, so their letters are put into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A body of soldiers turns out together for a celebrated sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TROOP with I (Roman numeral one).
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian investigator, among the best-known sleuths in fiction.

clue.text: Inflict loss on the man who pays road tax?

definitions.text: Inflict loss on the man who pays road tax?

parts.words: Inflict loss on the man who pays road tax?
parts.note: a phrase for causing damage, read literally as collecting a road charge from a motorist

explanation.definitionFit: To cause harm or depletion is idiomatically to exact a toll, and a tollkeeper literally collects such a charge from drivers.

clue.text: Finally succeeds in getting gold of course

definitions.text: Finally succeeds in getting gold of course

parts.words: Finally succeeds in getting gold of course
parts.note: describes winning the top award, with 'of course' hinting at a racecourse or golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Winning gold means coming top in a competition.

clue.text: Half a dozen Buddhists may go in for it

definitions.text: Buddhists may go in for it

indicators.note: the latter half of the five-letter word is taken, its final three letters

explanation.surface: Six monks might take up meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a' takes the back half of DOZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen is a school of Buddhism focused on meditation.

clue.text: Clearly not having a good complexion

definitions.text: Clearly not having a good complexion

parts.words: Clearly not having a good complexion
parts.note: describes skin visibly marked with patches, with 'Clearly' also hinting at the opposite of a clear complexion

explanation.definitionFit: Skin covered in red patches is described as blotchy.

clue.text: Small boy looking extremely nervous initially

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the three words that come before it

explanation.surface: A little lad appears very anxious at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Len is a short form of Leonard; 'Small boy' means a boy's name in short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Len is the diminutive of the male name Leonard.

clue.text: A girl about ten having sensory perception

indicators.note: the girl's name goes around the number, enclosing it

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman of about ten has a sixth sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an approximation of the girl's age, but it is the container signal; 'having' is a link, and an insect's antenna is its organ of sensory perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects' feelers are organs of touch and smell, giving them sensory perception.

clue.text: Dispiriting task for the clergy

parts.note: 'Dispiriting' read literally as driving out spirits, a rite a priest may perform

explanation.definitionFit: Casting out demons or evil spirits is a ritual carried out by priests.

clue.text: After a hundred years we have no fear!

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the numeral in the finished word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
what we have is ours, giving OUR
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A centenarian declares that a long life brings fearlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then OUR AGE ('years we have').
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery is the absence of fear.

clue.text: Perilously near to being taken in by Leo?

definitions.text: Perilously near to being taken in by Leo?

parts.words: Perilously near to being taken in by Leo?
parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac, so being swallowed by it puts one in grave danger

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a position of extreme danger, as if between a big cat's jaws.

clue.text: Literally given a title?

parts.note: a title is a heading, so something given one has a heading at the top

explanation.definitionFit: A page given a title bears a heading, which is how it is labelled.

clue.text: Tithes commuted for a sea goddess

indicators.note: a commuted payment is changed into another form, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Church dues are converted into payment for a marine deity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Thetis was a sea nymph, mother of Achilles.

clue.text: Not so enthusiastic about an item of kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the comparative wraps around the short word, enclosing it

parts.note: colder means less warm in feeling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is lukewarm about a new kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so enthusiastic' reads as describing someone's attitude, but it is a comparative synonym; 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl for draining food.

clue.text: Just nothing left in New York?

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: the two letters go in between the city's abbreviation letters

explanation.surface: Is there simply nothing remaining in the Big Apple?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O and L inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and merely are synonyms in the sense of 'nothing more than'.

clue.text: Joseph's mother coming in for a Chelsea bun

indicators.note: the name is tucked inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: Joseph's mum pops in to buy a sweet currant pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits inside 'foR A CHELsea bun'. A Chelsea bun is a British spiral currant roll.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Rachel, Jacob's wife, bore Joseph.

clue.text: A jacket of a sort, or only part of one, maybe

definitions.meaning: a record's cardboard cover, also called its jacket
the arm-covering part of a coat or jacket

explanation.definitionFit: A record cover is a kind of jacket, and the tube covering the arm is a piece of a jacket.

clue.text: An idol to follow around

indicators.note: turned around, the verb is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A star fan is told to trail their hero everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a worshipped image or deity.

clue.text: I get in the sun under the trees

indicators.note: the single letter is placed into the Latin word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: I lie in the sunshine beneath the woodland canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get in' puts I inside SOL. 'under the trees' defines it: soil is what lies beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth or ground lies beneath woodland, so soil is what is beneath the trees.
